findings.title: The keydown handler still removes aria-activedescendant on a bare Ctrl press, so the reported bug remains.
findings.body: The PR description says this handler now skips the removal for Ctrl/Shift/Alt/Meta, but the only change here is a comment. Pressing Ctrl alone still runs `inputBox.removeAttribute('aria-activedescendant')`. That moves the screen reader back to the input, which is how it re-announces "Type the command to run" (issue #271032 step 4). The description's second change is also missing: lines 222 and 263 still set the attribute to `''` instead of removing it. Add the modifier-key check described (`e.keyCode !== KeyCode.Ctrl && ...`), and call `removeAttribute` when `getActiveDescendant()` returns nothing.

findings.title: Skipping aria-activedescendant updates while Ctrl is held breaks Ctrl-held quick navigation for screen readers.
findings.body: The new `!this.keyMods.ctrlCmd` guard (here and the same one at line 262 for the tree) skips every focus update while Ctrl/Cmd is down, not just a lone Ctrl press. Several common flows move focus with Ctrl held: Ctrl+Tab editor switching, pressing Ctrl+P / Ctrl+E repeatedly in quick open (quickNavigate), and Ctrl+N/Ctrl+P or Ctrl+J/K list bindings. In those flows `aria-activedescendant` either stays on the old item or stays removed (the keydown handler removes it), so a screen reader never announces the newly focused item. Also, if the keyup is missed (for example on blur), `ctrlCmd` can stay true and block updates. Fix the root cause instead: in the keydown handler, don't remove the attribute when only a modifier key is pressed, and leave focus-change updates alone.

findings.title: The new test asserts nothing (`assert.ok(true)`).
findings.body: The test only checks that setting the placeholder doesn't throw. It never reads the input's `aria-label` and never checks whether the attribute was rewritten, so it passes whether or not the deduplication in `QuickInputBox` works. Assert on the input element's `aria-label`, or spy on `setAttribute` to confirm a same-value assignment doesn't touch the DOM.
